The '''Anesaki Kofun Group''' ({{ill|Anesaki Kofun Group|ja|姉崎古墳群}}, Anesaki Kofun-gun) is a cluster of {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|qid=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} (ancient Kofuns) located along the southern banks of the {{ill|Yōrō River|en|Yōrō River|qid=Q8062667|lt=Yōrō River}} in {{ill|Ichihara, Chiba|en|Ichihara, Chiba|qid=Q207881|lt=Ichihara, Chiba}}, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|qid=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}. The kofun date from the late {{ill|4th century|af|4de eeu|als|4. == Overview ==
A total of 34 kofun have been identified within the Anesaki Kofun Group, including 11 keyhole-shaped kofun, 2 square-keyhole kofun, 20 round kofun, and 1 square kofun. Many of the original mounds have been lost over time. Among the most prominent structures is the {{ill|Anegasaki Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|姉崎天神山古墳}}, the largest early-period keyhole-shaped kofun in the {{ill|Bōsō Peninsula|en|Bōsō Peninsula|qid=Q1022115|lt=Bōsō Peninsula}} region, measuring 130 meters in length. Nearby, the {{ill|Anesaki Futago-zuka Kofun|ja|姉崎二子塚古墳}} stands on sandy plains and measures 103 meters in length. 
Approximately 600 meters west of the Anesaki Tenjinyama Kofun lies the {{ill|Anesaki Shrine|ja|姉埼神社|sv|Anesaki-jinja}}, believed to have been established by the {{ill|Shanghai-kamiko|ja|上海上国造}} clan, a local ruling family. South of the shrine is the 86-meter-long Shakazan Kofun, while the now-destroyed 69-meter-long Sannōzan Kofun once stood roughly 100 meters to the west. The {{ill|Rokusonōbara Kofun|ja|六孫王原古墳|qid=Q140445996}}, located 600 meters south of the Anesaki Tenjinyama Kofun, is a square-keyhole-shaped mound with a corridor-style stone chamber facing south.
The earliest kofun in this group is believed to be the Anesaki Tenjinyama Kofun, dating to the early to mid-{{ill|4th century|af|4de eeu|als|4. The middleperiod is represented by the Anesaki Futago-zuka Kofun, dating to the late {{ill|5th century|en|5th century|qid=Q8095|lt=5th century}}. However, few middle-period keyhole-shaped kofun have been identified in the region. During the late period, the Sannōzan Kofun (early {{ill|6th century|en|6th century|qid=Q8090|lt=6th century}}) and the Rokusonōbara Kofun (late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|qid=Q8089|lt=7th century}}) were constructed. By the late period, the decline of prominent local chiefs such as the Shanghai-kamiko clan is evident in the lack of substantial funerary goods and the reduced map_size of the kofun.
